provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The original rule is out = transpose(in), a reflection across the main diagonal. Under a D4 transform T, the visible rule becomes T composed with the transpose composed with the inverse of T. Conjugating the main-diagonal reflection by a 90-degree rotation, or by a horizontal mirror, turns it into the anti-diagonal reflection. A 180-degree rotation leaves it unchanged. So d4 values 0, 2, 5 and 7 keep the main-diagonal reflection, out[i][j] = in[j][i]. Values 1, 3, 4 and 6 use the anti-diagonal reflection, out[i][j] = in[h-1-j][w-1-i]. As a check for d4=4: out' = fliplr(in^T), so out'[i][j] = in[n-1-j][i] = in'[n-1-j][n-1-i]. The emitted program builds the reflected grid row by row in visible coordinates, with no rotate-back wrapper. The rule only moves cells and never recolours them, so the palette has no role.
draft_notes.limitations: The orientation is set by d4 alone and the program does not check it against the demonstrations. The generator only produces square grids (size 3 by default). Rectangular inputs are still handled with a w-by-h output, which goes beyond the constructor's domain. There are no ties or background roles to resolve, and no constructor defects were found. The fixtures match the uniform transpose rule.
